Article Text:

India are set to get a major boost ahead of the T20I series against Afghanistan starting later this month. All-rounders Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy are on track as of now, while Washington Sundar is nearing the necessary clearances for the fixtures starting September 13 in Delhi. It is reliably learnt that Reddy has been training intensely at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) and operating at full capacity in order to return to international cricket.As for Washington Sundar, he spent the weekend in Chennai and will report back to the CoE this week to prove his fitness before selection. The men's senior selection committee chaired by Ajit Agarkar is likely to meet this week to pick the squad for the three T20Is."The practical target is the T20Is against Afghanistan and this will allow Washington Sundar to ease back into the set-up with the shortest format. His workload has gradually increased in the last few weeks, and he could be available for selection for the three T20Is," says a source tracking developments."Both Reddy and Pandya have been at the CoE for a very long time now and only take breaks for personal commitments.Reddy only goes back home during the weekends while Pandya has anyway moved base to Bengaluru," adds the source.All eyes, however, are on Jasprit Bumrah . The fast bowler missed the two Tests against Sri Lanka earlier this month and the management wants to handle him very carefully with an eye on the two Tests against New Zealand later this year. The 32-year-old has been training at the CoE. While the Afghanistan T20Is could be touch-and-go, the Asian Games shouldn't face any availability issues if there are no late hiccups during his rehabilitation."Bumrah is progressing well. In buildup to the 2027 World Cup, the plan was that he would focus on ODIs and Tests but since the knee injury, the management wants to ease him back with the shortest format first. He is being closely monitored and while the Afghanistan T20Is could be too close for comfort, the Asian Games seem highly likely, provided there are no late surprises," explains the source.After the recent outings in Ireland and England, the Indian team management is exploring options of left-arm spinners in the shortest format. Axar Patel played all seven games and had mediocre returns: two wickets in four T20Is against England and two wickets in two T20Is against Ireland. Krunal Pandya is being discussed, and his return to the T20I squad would not be a surprise.Krunal, who last played for India in 2021 T20 series against Sri Lanka, has been very impressive in the IPL and picked up 14 wickets for the Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the 2026 edition. It now remains to be seen whether the selectors revert to a proven performer as they look to find the right candidate for the crucial left-arm spinner spot.
Article Summary: India set to get a major boost ahead of the T20I series against Afghanistan. All-rounders Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy are on track as of now. Washington Sundar is nearing the necessary clearances for the fixtures starting September 13.

Article Title: IPL media rights: Does the BCCI have a Plan B?
Article Text:
IPL Trophy (Photo Credit: BCCI/IPL)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Indian cricket board's reluctance to seek better price discovery ahead of the upcoming IPL and home bilateral media rights tender is weighing heavily on the industry.With about six months to go before the final IPL edition of the 2023-27 rights cycle begins, there is growing concern among cricket's biggest stakeholders that the absence of a credible bidder other than JioStar will prevent an accurate assessment of the property's value, and, in turn, deny the market the competitive tension that has driven IPL rights upwards for a decade.That sentiment was echoed by none other than Uday Shankar, the media entrepreneur who serves as vice-chairman of JioStar, at the recent ET World Leaders Forum."Ten years ago, you would have multiple and serious media companies (around four) competing for major sports rights. You'd have four or more companies genuinely fighting for properties. Today, increasingly, it feels as if we are the only ones standing. And that's not healthy," Shankar said."The fundamental issue is that the cost of the rights has risen dramatically. But the ability to monetise those rights hasn't necessarily risen at the same rate. The value of sports is enormous, but the rights holder, broadcaster and platform all need to participate in a sustainable ecosystem," he added.The worrying part of this narrative is the absence of a Plan B for Indian cricket. That JioStar will bid healthily for the IPL is a given: its subscription numbers are heavily leveraged against cricket consumption.What is baffling is the BCCI's inability to bring more participants to the table.Players such as YouTube and Netflix have been engaging aggressively with sport in the West. YouTube's move into rights aggregation and bundling has, in fact, become an industry trend of its own.YouTube increasingly treats sport not as a series of standalone rights acquisitions but as the anchor of a broader pay-TV and subscription ecosystem. Its seven-year deal for exclusive US distribution of NFL Sunday Ticket — worth a reported $2 billion a season — works both as a value-add for YouTube TV subscribers and as a standalone product sold through YouTube channels.Average revenue per user in the West bears little resemblance to what the subcontinent generates, which complicates the assumption that volume alone wins the argument. Even so, Indian cricket remains the only market in this part of the world worth a player like YouTube testing the waters in.More recently, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos told The Economic Times that the streaming giant was interested in live sport, including cricket, but had no intention of becoming a "conventional full-season sports broadcaster".If so, a property like the IPL sits squarely in Netflix's territory. The storytelling potential of an India-first sports property speaks to a billion-plus domestic audience, a vast global diaspora, and to markets where cricket remains one of India's most effective exports and a quiet instrument of soft power."At some point, the economics have to make sense," Shankar says. For that to happen, the responsibility must lie with the federation itself to market what is, by any measure, a high-value product.The IPL may be India's most prized prime-time asset. But to assume that a media player several time zones away is fully clued in to the India story, without hearing it first-hand from the people writing it, is optimistic at best.Which is why it matters that the BCCI arrives at this tender with a genuine marketing strategy: one that puts the IPL in front of the dozens of media, technology and streaming platforms worldwide that could plausibly be interested.JioStar is the BCCI's Plan A. The question is whether there is a Plan B, or a Plan C.
Article Summary: The Indian cricket board's reluctance to seek better price discovery ahead of the upcoming IPL and home bilateral media rights tender is weighing heavily on the industry. There is growing concern among cricket's biggest stakeholders that the absence of a credible bidder will prevent an accurate assessment of the property's value.

Article Title: 'Praggnanandhaa is No. 1 in the world': Viswanathan Anand after India's first Grand Chess Tour title | Exclusive
Article Text:
R Praggnanandhaa and Viswanathan Anand

A family photo after Vaishali's Women's Candidates win (Tushar Damor/ChessBase India)

I think at the moment, I would say he (Pragg) is the number one player in the world. Viswanathan Anand, former five-time World Chess Champion

R Praggnanandhaa (Photo by Lennart Ootes)

NEW DELHI: You remember the photo that made rounds on social media last April, just after Vaishali Rameshbabu, Praggnanandhaa's elder sister, had landed at the Chennai airport with the Women's Candidates medal wrapped around her neck. It was a photo of her family.Praggnanandhaa was there too, his facial gesture mirroring anything but the sorrow of an underwhelming campaign in the open category of the Candidates, his hand holding a placard congratulating his sister on her homecoming.If that was Vaishali's moment, Praggnanandhaa's is now.Late Thursday in St Louis, he beat Fabiano Caruana 15-13 to win the Grand Chess Tour (GCT) Finals, becoming the first Indian and only the seventh player in the tournament's 11-year history to do it The prize money was $200,000. But even more than the prize money, it is about a 21-year-old who somewhat imploded at the 2026 Candidates and now sits, by one of the sport's most respected judges, at the top of the world.During an interaction with TimesofIndia.com, Viswanathan Anand , who is set to return to the board with Alaskan Knights for the new season of the Global Chess League (GCL) this September, assessed Praggnanandhaa's turnaround since that Candidates low."During the Candidates, he was having a kind of slump," the former five-time World Chess Champion said. "His play had already started to decline at the end of last year, compared to the first half, but in the Candidates, it was really not very impressive.And then I thought he must have been a bit gloomy."What followed, in Anand's telling, was something closer to a pattern than a one-off recovery."In Norway Chess, he was not doing well. At some point, there were four rounds left, and he was in the bottom. And then he won four games in a row," Anand explained. "He did something similar here, though his performance was much better in Grand Chess Tour and also in the Rapid. He won the Rapid, did well enough in the Blitz to win the tournament. Then he was sort of competing for first place here."It's the shape of these comebacks that Anand keeps returning to. "He has this capacity, and it's becoming more and more noticeable that he's able to win late games and change everything," he remarked. "And that's a very, very rare skill and useful skill to have."Then came the line that will follow Praggnanandhaa into the Olympiad next month. "I think at the moment, I would say he's the number one player in the world," Anand told this website with utmost authority."Well, Magnus doesn't compete in the same events, but nonetheless, you know, if you take classical included, and I know Pragg, in the tournaments which happened in August and all, he performed incredibly well. If you go back to Norway Chess and then see the development from there, I think it's just fantastic."It's not an idle comparison. Praggnanandhaa's road to St Louis ran through 27 rapid and blitz games, nine classical games, and 16 more across the semifinals and final. He arrived having already beaten Magnus Carlsen twice in classical chess in Norway earlier this year, including a stretch of four straight classical wins to close out Oslo.In the GCT final itself, he lost the opening classical game to Caruana and fumbled a likely equaliser in the second before finding his footing, winning both rapid games to seize control, then holding the four-game blitz section to a 4-4 draw to close it out.He'd already avenged a bruising from World Championship Challenger Javokhir Sindarov, who beat him twice at the Cyprus Candidates, by finishing joint-first with him at the Sinquefield Cup.ALSO READ: Praggnanandhaa’s invisible second: The making of Vaibhav Suri He'd been beaten there by Vincent Keymer, too, before eliminating the German in the GCT semifinal.For a player whose technical range and universal style have long had experts rating him the most complete of India's young elite, the Candidates collapse had looked like the one gap in the resume. St Louis just closed it, in front of the one man whose word on the subject still carries the most weight in Indian chess.
Article Summary: R Praggnanandhaa won the Grand Chess Tour (GCT) Finals on Thursday. He is the first Indian and only the seventh player in the tournament's 11-year history to do it. He beat Fabiano Caruana 15-13 to win the tournament in St Louis.

Article Title: ‘Social media player’: Ex-Pakistan cricketer brutally tears into Babar Azam after Lord’s horror show
Article Text:
Babar Azam (ANI Photo)

Basit questions Babar’s Test record

Saud Shakeel also comes under fire

Pakistan’s batting collapses again

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan batter Basit Ali has launched a strong criticism of Babar Azam after the Pakistan captain endured another disappointing outing in the second Test against England at Lord’s.Pakistan suffered a 194-run defeat on Sunday to concede the three-match series 2-0, with their batting once again failing to withstand pressure. Chasing 389 in the fourth innings, Pakistan were bowled out for 194, while Babar managed only six after scoring eight in the first innings.For Basit, Babar’s latest failure raised a much bigger question about his contribution when Pakistan need him most.Speaking on The Game Plan show, Basit compared Babar with several legendary Pakistan batters, arguing that the country’s greatest players established their reputations by delivering in difficult situations.“They didn't become great players just like that. I'm not even talking about Sachin Tendulkar. I'm talking about my own countrymen".Basit then questioned whether Babar has done enough when Pakistan have been under pressure.“When you don't do anything in difficult times, what's the point? You're a great player in your fan following. You're a great player in front of social media.”The former batter then directly turned his attention to Babar and highlighted his long wait for a Test century.Babar’s last Test hundred came in December 2022, when he scored 161 against New Zealand in Karachi. Since then, he has been unable to reach three figures in the format.“When will you do it? I'm talking about Babar [Azam]. I'll take his name. He hasn't scored a [Test] hundred in four years. When will you do it?” Basit said.He also expressed his frustration at Babar’s dismissal at Lord’s, particularly because Pakistan’s batting heavily relied on their captain to provide a substantial contribution.“It's a matter of pain. When the entire country's batting depends on you. At least don't get out by hitting such a shot,” Basit lamented.Babar’s dismissal came early in the chase when he got into trouble against Jofra Archer. The Pakistan captain attempted to leave a short delivery but ended up offering a simple catch to Jordan Cox in the slip cordon.Basit did not spare the other Pakistan batters either. Saud Shakeel provided the strongest resistance during the chase, scoring 97 off 132 balls and helping Pakistan recover after they slipped to 14/3. However, his attempt to accelerate towards a century ultimately cost him his wicket.After smashing two sixes in an over from Josh Tongue, Shakeel fell three runs short of his hundred while attempting another aggressive shot.“I'm not even satisfied with Saud [Shakeel]'s shot. You've taken on five fielders and you're hitting such a shot,” Basit complained.Mohammad Rizwan was another target of Basit’s criticism after the wicketkeeper-batter scored only one before being dismissed lbw by Ollie Robinson.“What shot did [Mohammad] Rizwan hit? Doesn't he have any sense? Is he playing a Test match or street cricket?” Basit said.Pakistan’s problems with the bat were evident almost immediately in their chase.Robinson dismissed Azan Awais lbw before producing a delivery that breached Abdullah Shafique’s defence and hit the off stump, leaving Pakistan in serious trouble.Archer then removed Babar, and Pakistan went into lunch with Saud Shakeel and Shan Masood attempting to rebuild.Shakeel eventually reached his fifty from 54 balls and formed a useful partnership with Masood. But Robinson returned after the rain interruption to dismiss Masood, before removing Rizwan soon afterwards.With Imam-ul-Haq unavailable to bat because of his calf injury, Pakistan’s hopes were effectively over. Shakeel continued fighting but fell on 97, with Tongue then wrapping up the tail.England’s bowlers dominated the final innings, with Robinson finishing with eight wickets in the match, as Pakistan were dismissed for 194.The defeat leaves Pakistan 2-0 down in the series, with the third and final Test to be played at Edgbaston in Birmingham from September 9.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan batter Basit Ali criticises Babar Azam on The Game Plan. Babar has not scored a Test hundred in four years. Basit also criticises Saud Shakeel and Mohammad Rizwan. Pakistan were bowled out for 194 in their fourth innings at Lord's.

Article Title: Manchester City make shock move to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool in £85m deal: Reports
Article Text:
Manchester City have opened talks for Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo, with reports valuing the Dutchman at £85m/ Image: X

Why could Gakpo leave Liverpool?

Gakpo has been an important part of Liverpool's attack

City preparing for a busy finish to the window

Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool over a potential move for Cody Gakpo, with the Dutch forward emerging as one of the biggest names who could still change clubs before the transfer window closes.According to reports, City made formal contact with Liverpool on Saturday evening regarding a move for the 27-year-old. ESPN, citing its own sources, reported that discussions between the clubs had gathered pace and that Liverpool value Gakpo at £85 million ($115m).Gakpo has also attracted interest from Tottenham Hotspur, but sources cited by BBC Sport indicate that Manchester City is the forward's preferred destination should he leave Anfield.The possibility of Gakpo's departure comes at a particularly interesting point in Liverpool's transfer window. The Reds have agreed a deal to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola for a fee that could rise to £123 million, according to BBC Sport, and Liverpool are understood to want another forward through the door before allowing Gakpo to leave.Liverpool have an interest in Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace forward Ismaïla Sarr, with the club having already seen bids for both players rejected, according to reports.That means Gakpo's situation is not simply a matter of whether City are prepared to meet Liverpool's valuation; the Reds also need to make sure they have sufficient attacking options before sanctioning his exit.ESPN reported that City have been encouraged by Gakpo's interest in a move to the Etihad Stadium and are pressing ahead with negotiations.Gakpo joined Liverpool from his boyhood club PSV Eindhoven in January 2023 and has since scored 33 goals in 91 Premier League appearances.The forward has also started the new season in good form. He scored in Liverpool's opening league fixture, a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United, and then provided the assist for Alexander Isak's goal in Saturday's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest at Anfield.Gakpo started against Forest despite the growing speculation surrounding his future, with Liverpool twice having to come from behind to rescue a point.His possible departure would therefore leave Andoni Iraola with another significant attacking decision to make, particularly with Liverpool already close to bringing Barcola into the squad.Manchester City are also expected to remain active during the final days of the transfer window.According to ESPN, City have already agreed a deal with Palmeiras for Brazilian winger Allan, while Savio and Omar Marmoush have both left the club to join Tottenham this summer.The club have also been working on their midfield, having already spent more than £200 million on that area following the departures of Bernardo Silva and Rodri, with Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi among their additions.ESPN's sources say City are expected to make at least one late bid for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernández as well as continuing discussions over Gakpo.For Liverpool, meanwhile, the decision is becoming increasingly time-sensitive, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday, September 1. The club must now weigh City's interest against its own need to maintain numbers in attack, particularly with Barcola's arrival close and further moves for Minteh or Sarr still being pursued.
Article Summary: Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool over a potential move for Cody Gakpo. The Dutch forward could still change clubs before the transfer window closes. Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola for a fee of £123 million.

Article Title: Michael Carrick says it is ‘lazy’ to claim Man Utd lacked passion after embarrassing 2-0 defeat to newly promoted Hull City
Article Text:
Manchester United's interim head coach Michael Carrick walks on the pitch at the end of the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester United and Nottingham Forest in Manchester, England, Sunday, May 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson)

Carrick rejects claims United lacked desire

Carrick wants United to respond

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Michael Carrick has dismissed suggestions that Manchester United lacked passion or motivation in their shock opening-day defeat to newly promoted Hull City, calling it “lazy” to reduce the performance to a lack of effort.United began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-0 defeat at the MKM Stadium despite having 71.7% possession, with Hull scoring twice from set pieces in the first half. The result has led to criticism of United's attitude and desire, but Carrick insists there was more to the defeat than simply a failure to try.United were accused of lacking passion and intensity during the defeat, but Carrick defended his players ahead of Sunday's home meeting with another newly promoted side, Ipswich Town.“Teams lose games and win games, and it's not just because you try or you don't try,” Carrick told a news conference.“There are all sorts of different reasons. Teams lose games, so there's different reasons. I don't have to give you the total reason, because we know what we're trying to improve on.“I think it's so easy and lazy to just say 'team loses a game, everything's wrong.' This is wrong, this is wrong, not trying enough, not enough passion.”Carrick's comments come after a difficult start in which United dominated possession but struggled to turn that control into enough attacking threat, while two first-half set-piece goals left them chasing the game.United now have the chance to respond immediately when Ipswich visit Old Trafford on Sunday for the club's first home match of the season.Carrick lost only two Premier League games last season, against Leeds United and Newcastle United, and United responded with victories on both occasions. The club went on to finish third in the Premier League in 2025-26, with 20 wins, 11 draws and seven defeats.For Carrick, how his players respond to the Hull setback will say more about them than the defeat itself.“I think success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end,” Carrick added.“In any position, certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there's going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others.“I think it ultimately decides what type of team you're going to become. So far, we've dealt with those setbacks really well, within games, game to game.“We had one last week. No getting away from it and it's disappointing. But we look to bounce back. We had a good week, boys are refocused, learned from where we could have improved, and keep pushing forward.”
Article Summary: Michael Carrick has dismissed suggestions that Manchester United lacked passion or motivation in their shock opening-day defeat to newly promoted Hull City. United began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-0 defeat at the MKM Stadium. The result has led to criticism of United's attitude and desire, but Carrick insists there was more to the defeat than simply a failure to try.

Article Title: 'That's a joke': Nasser Hussain slams umpires' decision to abandon England vs Pakistan Day 3 at Lord's
Article Text:
Rain at Lord's

England in control as debate continues

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The decision to end play early on the third day of England’s second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s has sparked criticism after the weather improved soon after the umpires called it off.Rain had disrupted most of Saturday, with the morning session completely washed out and only 24.5 overs possible. Players left the field at 17:08 BST, when conditions still looked poor. But the rain soon stopped, the sky became brighter and ground staff began removing some of the covers.Despite this, umpires Paul Reiffel and Allahuddien Parker abandoned the day at 18:30, with around an hour of scheduled play still available. Some fans booed the decision, while former England captain Nasser Hussain strongly criticised it."That's a joke, honestly a joke," former England captain Hussain said on Sky Sports."I earlier said how good the umpires have been. These fans have waited all afternoon for it to stop raining. It's now bright. There's blue sky in the distance. That is an unbelievable decision, it really is."In about five minutes' time it's going to be sunny here."The weather stayed dry until the scheduled close at 19:30. Because fewer than 30 overs were played, spectators will receive a 50% ticket refund.England finished the day on 177-7, holding a 357-run lead and looking well placed to win the match and series. Dan Lawrence, unbeaten on 50, said returning for only 40 minutes would not have been ideal."It would have been a tricky 40 minutes to go out there and bat," said Dan Lawrence, who made an unbeaten 50."It's nice to have a good sleep and think about how I'm going to play in the morning. I can imagine it will be with the same intent and trying to push the game forward."Forty minutes of batting at 6.45pm is never an ideal thing."The controversy came alongside a similar situation in the County Championship, where Durham were unable to chase four runs against Gloucestershire because of bad light.
Article Summary: England finish day on 177-7, holding a 357-run lead over Pakistan. Players left the field at 17:08 BST, when conditions still looked poor. But the rain soon stopped, the sky became brighter and ground staff began removing some of the covers. Some fans booed the decision, while former England captain Nasser Hussain strongly criticised it.

With the scores tied at 3-3, the match went into a penalty shootout and Belgium came out triumphant 4-3 as India’s men’s team finished a disappointing eighth in the FIH World Cup.Seasoned campaigner Vincent Vanasch showcased why he is considered among the best goalkeepers in the world. Article Title: ‘We have to do it over and over’: Sjoerd Marijne on India’s next challenge

Kolkata: India’s best World Cup finish in 52 years has given the women’s hockey team a significant boost in confidence, but coach Sjoerd Marijne believes the real challenge is to sustain that level. In an exclusive conversation with TOI, the Dutchman reflected on India’s campaign, the team’s growing discipline and belief, and the challenges ahead at the Asian Games. Excerpts...I think the discipline, the structure, the talent, the belief and working as a unit made the difference. From the moment we started, we said, ‘You have to dream big, you have to believe, but the discipline needs to be really high, and you have to think about the team.’From the beginning until now, I have seen them enjoying themselves more. They are having fun with each other, they are bonding, and they understand the culture and what we want to achieve.The most important thing is that we believe more in ourselves and we have proven that we can do it.It’s not just about saying we can do it; we actually did it. I can always refer to matches — how close we were against Netherlands, how well we did and how we created field chances against them. If you can do it against them, you can do it against every country.We did really well in the tournament, but it doesn’t say anything about the future. We have to see in Pro League whether we can consistently bring this level to every match. The fact that we now beat Germany doesn’t mean we are always going to beat them. The girls have seen that we can do it. I don’t have to tell them anymore because we have proven we can do it. But now we have to do it over and over.I know the expectations are higher. Of course, after the World Cup, everybody now expects more, and so do the girls. That’s fine. It’s normal. But we also have to learn to deal with that, and we have to focus on ourselves. That’s an important one for me.It’s a combination. It’s not only about the juniors. The juniors are supported by the seniors and the experienced players. If the seniors don’t perform well, the juniors can’t perform well. It starts with the seniors. They are guiding the younger players in the culture I want to establish in the team.All credit goes to Wayne Lombard and his team, the physios and the masseuse. It’s all on them. I follow their plan 100%. If they say we need to train more calmly, we train more calmly. If we need to train harder, we train harder.I go 100% with their vision, and that worked in the past and is working now as well.Not at all. Every time we had penalty corners, Deepika was out. We tried a few variations, and Navneet was there at the right moments. For me, it’s not a concern. The next step for us is to get more penalty corners. If you look at our percentage, it can be higher in terms of winning PCs and then getting more opportunities to execute them.
Article Summary: India's best World Cup finish in 52 years has given the women’s hockey team a significant boost in confidence. Coach Sjoerd Marijne believes the real challenge is to sustain that level. In an exclusive conversation with TOI, the Dutchman reflected on India's campaign, the team's growing discipline and belief.

Article Title: Carlos Alcaraz returns to US Open after four-month injury layoff with tennis world watching
Article Text:
Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New York City: Four months is a long time in tennis.Since Carlos Alcaraz injured his right wrist in a fateful moment in mid-April, the men’s tour, like the swirling seasons, has changed.Alexander Zverev won his first Grand Slam title at 29 during a fortnight when temperatures soared at Roland Garros, while world No. 1 Jannik Sinner defended his Wimbledon title. Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar shot up the ATP rankings, climbing from outside the top 500 to the brink of the world’s top 10 in less than a year.It is into this unpredictable landscape that a new-look Alcaraz walks in. The 23-year-old, however, will take comfort from the fact that he returns to competitive tennis at the US Open, the Grand Slam where it all began for him.It was at this sprawling venue in New York’s Queens borough in 2022 that he claimed his maiden major crown and climbed to No. 1 in the rankings for the first time. It was here that he returned to the pinnacle again last year, defeating Sinner to claim his second US Open title.On Monday, Alcaraz, whose long, flowy locks, held back by a thin black headband, have already attracted plenty of wows from the fandom, opens against Roman Safiullin, the 29-year-old who lit up Wimbledon with his fight last month.The Russian also defeated Alcaraz in straight sets at the Paris Masters three years ago.The two most recent Masters 1000 champions, Ben Shelton and Arthur Fils, are potential quarterfinal opponents for second-seeded Alcaraz, who has 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic in his half.“I’m feeling great,” Alcaraz told international media at his pre-championship conference. “I think that right now it’s (injury) all in my head. I gotta trust my team, I gotta trust my people that tell me it’s gonna be fine. So I just have to go 100%, and stay away from that fear.”“My team and I believe that I’m ready,” he added. “It wasn’t an easy decision. I did whatever it took to be ready. I tried to do everything perfect on and off the court, really long practices, intense practices, just to see how my wrist is going to react.”Alcaraz practised with the 23-year-old Holger Rune, the big-hitting former No. 4, in Murcia before arriving in New York.Even though Alcaraz enters the US Open after a four-month injury break and without a prior hard-court singles match, the second seed is hardly short of expectations. If anything, the last few months have underlined just how much Alcaraz, Sinner and the 39-year-old Djokovic matter to the men’s game.They are the sport’s biggest stars, the ones who put bums on seats. At Roland Garros in May-June, with Alcaraz out of tournament play and Sinner’s challenge wilting in the heat, Zverev’s title run became an uncomfortable one for the sport. The German’s two separate sets of domestic abuse allegations reshaped the way he has been covered in parts of the media.Now, with Sinner out with a dodgy right knee, the onus to carry the load for his generation falls on Alcaraz.Daniil Medvedev, the 30-year-old world No. 8, argued that if Alcaraz is at Flushing Meadows, it means he and his team are confident that the wrist has sufficiently recovered.“I don’t think the wrist is going to be a problem,” he said. “It’s more for the whole body itself. If he has a tough match, it could be interesting to see how he copes. It’s really nice for me to see him here to play. If I have a chance, I’m going to watch his match, he’s playing my friend Roman.”
Article Summary: Carlos Alcaraz returns to competitive tennis at the US Open. The 23-year-old injured his right wrist in a fateful moment in mid-April. It was at this venue in New York’s Queens borough that he claimed his maiden major crown.

Article Title: US Open: Aryna Sabalenka’s New York test is about more than No. 1
Article Text:
Aryna Sabalenka (Getty Images)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW YORK CITY: Aryna Sabalenka arrived at Flushing Meadows chasing history. She could leave it without the No. 1 ranking.The 28-year-old two-time defending champion is chasing history, aiming to become the first woman since Serena Williams (2012-14) to win three straight US Open titles. But her dip in form has left her hold on the No. 1 ranking looking increasingly fragile. Sabalenka, who made the final of the Australian Open in January and won back-to-back WTA 1000 titles in Indian Wells and Miami has made just one semifinal in her last seven tournaments. The powerful Belarusian, whose recent meltdowns have left spectators gasping, is 17-7 since April.The top seed is closing in on a significant milestone -- 100 consecutive weeks at No. 1 -- but would need to win a third straight US Open title to get there. Sabalenka will reach 99 weeks atop the rankings by the end of the tournament, but with the 2,000 points from last year's title coming off her tally and three players in position to overtake her, extending her reign for another week is no longer entirely in her hands.Elena Rybakina, who clinched the title at Melbourne Park to give her season a rousing start, is less than 500 points behind Sabalenka in the WTA rankings.But the 27-year-old Kazakh’s run into the year’s final Grand Slam has been hampered by a left-ankle injury. Still, the second-seeded Rybakina could rise to No. 1 without playing a match at the US Open, provided Sabalenka, Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff do not win the title. Should Rybakina reach the semifinals, however, the top ranking is hers regardless of the other results.Sabalenka will bring a little New York spunk to court, kitted out in a basketball-inspired mesh dress with white seams over a bright orange sports bra and matching shorts. Her jewellery -- necklace, bracelet and drop earrings carrying more than 127 carats of coloured gemstones -- channels the city's bold, multicultural spirit. Whether that swagger carries over to her tennis, however, remains the bigger question, as the top seed begins her title defence on Monday against Camila Osorio.At her pre-tournament media briefing, when Sabalenka was asked about her recent run in tournaments, that has left much of the fandom wondering, what’s wrong with Aryna, the world No.1, replied with a smile, “maybe there's something wrong with people.”When tapped about her confidence levels she replied, always confident, before expanding. “That's the beauty of sport, throw tough challenges at me and I will come back only stronger,” she said.There were warning signs in Paris of the world No.1’s struggles. At Roland Garros, Sabalenka was within touching distance of the semifinals, leading Russia's Diana Shnaider 6-3, 5-3, when her game suddenly deserted her. She dropped the final 10 games to lose 6-3, 5-7, 0-6, a collapse as startling as it was troubling.“It wasn't the best period. I don't want to defend myself, but obviously I just don't want to talk about that period,” she said of the last four months. “I've been dealing with several things, but who cares, right? Yeah, I didn't perform my best.”“These tough lessons are definitely going to make me stronger and work even harder,” she finished.The top seed’s outfit may scream New York, but the message from Sabalenka's season is quieter, nothing can be taken for granted. The defending champion may have history in sight, but not everything is in her hands, courtesy of leads she has squandered. In Flushing Meadows, she will need more than her trademark power. It is never about one week or one tournament, it is about finding a way to stay standing when the pressure starts to bite, and carrying that resilience into the homestretch of the 2026 season.
Article Summary: Aryna Sabalenka aiming to become first woman since Serena Williams to win three straight US Open titles. Top seed is closing in on a significant milestone -- 100 consecutive weeks at No. 1. Belarusian has made just one semifinal in her last seven tournaments and is 17-7 since April. She begins her title defence on Monday against Camila Osorio.

Article Title: 'I felt sorry for the guy': Eight years later, Faf du Plessis revisits one of cricket’s darkest chapters; 'Sandpaper Gate', and believes Australia handled the scandal poorly
Article Text:
Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft

Du Plessis questions Australia’s response

Faf says bans were unnecessary

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Eight years after the Sandpaper Gate scandal shook Australian cricket, former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has offered a different perspective on one of the most controversial episodes in the sport. Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper to alter the ball during the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa, setting off a scandal that engulfed the Australian team. Steve Smith and David Warner were also punished, with all three players losing their leadership positions or facing lengthy suspensions.But du Plessis believes Bancroft, in particular, was subjected to an unnecessarily harsh media trial. Speaking to former South Africa pacer Vernon Philander on the ‘Beyond the Boundary’ podcast, he said his immediate reaction was sympathy for the young Australian batter.“Bancroft, and honestly, my first instincts with him were, I felt sorry for the guy. When I saw him, first of all, he did that, and I was like, ‘Shame.’ He doesn't know what to do. He doesn't know how to get the ball to reverse swing, because taking a piece of sandpaper out of your pocket with cameras, it's not the most clever thing to do,” Faf said.The incident quickly escalated beyond the field. Du Plessis recalled how the South African team waited for Australia's press conference following the day's play, only to see the situation become even more explosive after the Australian team's statement.“Then it was that whole incident. I mean, we were sitting after the day's play. And we were like, the team is taking like an hour before the press conference has to start. So we're like, why are they taking so long? What are they doing? And then they issued that statement. And that statement was just like putting blitz under a fire and just going there. And they were saying, no one knows about it. The captain had no idea. The coach had no idea. And everyone was just like, well, hang on, what's going on here? Everyone knows what goes on in a dressing room,” he added.The scandal eventually saw Smith and Warner handed 12-month bans, while Bancroft was suspended for nine months. Smith and Warner were also removed from their leadership positions.Du Plessis believes Cricket Australia made the situation considerably bigger by allowing outside pressure, including political intervention, to influence its response.“So I think it was more the way that they handled that that caused a lot of noise. And then it went back to Australia, where the Australian Prime Minister got involved. The ex-cricketers were smashing the team about how you can do that? And we were sitting there going, come on, guys. It's not like you guys got a first to do it. You never did it. Like, don't be glasshouse,” said Faf.He also recalled reaching out to Smith during the fallout because he expected the punishment to last weeks or perhaps a month, rather than an entire year.“Everyone has done it at some stage in their career. Warner, Smith and Bancroft were the three guys who were actually caught. I felt the right thing to do was to send Steve Smith a message and say, Listen, I know you guys are trying to do the right thing. You're going to go through some crap over the next week. I thought it would be like a week or a month. But it ended up being a year. I was just like, I'm sorry you're going through this. You shouldn't take the brunt of this. It's a thing that, unfortunately, should fall on the whole team. But yeah, I felt for Bancroft. I felt sorry for him because he just didn't know how to do it. And Steve Smith for trying to do the right thing to be the captain and say, it's my show,” he added.Du Plessis went further, arguing that the players should not have been removed from international cricket for such long periods.In his view, the International Cricket Council should have handled the disciplinary side of the incident, while Cricket Australia could have imposed financial penalties instead of lengthy bans.“I think they could have handled that a little bit better. Cricket Australia had other ideas. And they made that thing become a very big thing. Just let the ICC deal with it. I think when you let politics and stuff come into sport, it never ends well. And that's the case with the Prime Minister's politics and everyone putting pressure on them. And they're feeling like they have to act. They have to act to show that they're doing something. I think that becomes a dangerous precedent,” said Faf.Du Plessis suggested that the punishment could instead have been limited to match-fee deductions, allowing the players to continue their careers without missing an entire year.“I think if they took it on the chin on that night and said, Cameron would have said, I'm sorry, I made it a bad thing. I'm young in international cricket, and I'm sorry. Which he obviously did.But I think he would have gotten a 50 per cent match fee from the ICC. Steve Smith would have played the next Test match. David Warner, they would have played the whole rest of the year. But what ended up happening is they missed a year of cricket,” he added.For du Plessis, the Sandpaper Gate scandal was therefore not only about what happened on the field, but also about how the aftermath was handled. He believes the punishment, political pressure and public reaction turned an already serious incident into a much bigger crisis for Smith, Warner and Bancroft.
Article Summary: Faf du Plessis says he felt sorry for Cameron Bancroft after he was caught using sandpaper to alter the ball during the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa. The former South Africa captain believes the Australian team was subjected to an unnecessarily harsh media trial. He believes Cricket Australia made the situation considerably bigger by allowing outside pressure, including political intervention, to influence its response.

Former Pakistan captain Rashid Latif has launched a furious attack on the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and its chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the national side suffered another heavy defeat against England at Lord’s.Pakistan were beaten by 194 runs in the second Test, giving England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. The visitors have struggled badly throughout the tour, particularly with the bat, and have offered little competition to England.The poor performances have reportedly led sections of the British media to label this Pakistan side the “worst Pakistan side in the last 50 years”. Latif agreed with the assessment but argued that the scrutiny should not stop with the players.Instead, the former wicketkeeper-batter pointed the finger at the PCB administration, selection committee and coaching staff, claiming the board itself had played a major role in the team’s decline.“Everyone is talking about the Pakistan team, and how it is the worst touring team in the last 50 years. But nobody is speaking about how the current board is the worst in the last 70 years. Nobody is talking about the worst selection committee and coaches,” Latif said on Geo News.“If you combine these issues, you will get the answer to your question. You will know who has ruined this team. Now you are losing consistently. This is the worst cricket board, that's a fact,” he added.Pakistan’s biggest problem during the series has been their batting. The visitors have failed to cross 200 even once in the series, leaving their bowlers with little margin for error. Babar Azam missed the opening Test but returned at Lord’s with hopes that his presence would provide stability to the struggling batting order. Instead, the Pakistan captain endured another difficult outing, scoring just 8 and 6.His second-innings dismissal was particularly disappointing, as Jofra Archer unsettled him with a sharp bouncer and made Babar appear uncomfortable against the short ball.Pakistan’s struggles have now become a major talking point as they prepare for the final Test.The Lord’s Test was also surrounded by an off-field dispute involving the PCB and Sky Sports.The broadcaster aired an 18-minute interview with Sulaiman and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran Khan. During the programme, they discussed their father’s circumstances and treatment while he remains in prison.Reports subsequently claimed that the PCB had threatened to pull Pakistan out of the Test if the interview was broadcast.However, both Babar and Pakistan head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed denied being aware of any such plan.The controversy ultimately did not affect the match, with Pakistan returning to the field as scheduled. England went on to secure a comprehensive victory and take the series.The two sides will now travel to Birmingham for the third and final Test at Edgbaston, beginning on September 9.

Article Title: West Zone coach Amit Dani wants Duleep Trophy’s knock-out format changed
Article Text:
Duleep Trophy (ANI Photo)

MUMBAI: When the Duleep Trophy semifinals began at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru on Sunday, 19-time champions West Zone were conspicuous by their absence.West crashed out after a 52-run defeat to North Zone in a low-scoring quarterfinal, with North posting 251 and 222, while West managed 187 and 234.Former Mumbai first-class cricketer Amit Dani, who coached West Zone this season, believes the tournament’s knockout format needs a rethink.“I suggested to the BCCI that it should seriously consider not having knockout matches until the final in the Duleep Trophy. It’s the first tournament of the season and players are often a bit rusty. Even if North Zone had been knocked out after just one game, it wouldn’t have been fair on their players either,” Dani told TOI.Dani argued that the current format limits opportunities for players and selectors alike.“The selectors wanted to watch Tanush Kotian, but they got to see him in only one match. It was a difficult wicket where the ball was gripping and turning, making batting tough. Players need more games. With the final scheduled only on Sept 6, there is room for one more league match,” he said.Despite the early exit, Dani found plenty of positives in West’s campaign.He reserved special praise for Musheer Khan, whose 96 in the fourth innings was the highest score of the match.“On that wicket, it was a top-quality knock. It wasn’t easy to bat there, but Musheer showed superb temperament and skill,” Dani said.He felt Anshul Kamboj’s brisk 60 in North’s first innings and Ruturaj Gaikwad’s run-out while batting on 66 in the chase proved decisive.“For us, Musheer, Tanush and Tushar Deshpande stood out. Tushar bowled with real fire and intensity. I hope all three are considered for India A or the Rest of India squad for the Irani Cup,” Dani added.
Article Summary: Former Mumbai first-class cricketer Amit Dani believes the tournament’s knockout format needs a rethink. West Zone crashed out after a 52-run defeat to North Zone in a low-scoring quarterfinal. Dani: "I suggested to the BCCI that it should seriously consider not having knockout matches until the final in the Duleep Trophy"

Article Text:

The International Cricket Council (ICC) has removed Sri Lanka’s hosting rights for the first-ever Women’s Champions Trophy, scheduled for 2027, because of concerns over government involvement in the running of Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC).The tournament was expected to feature six teams, including the host nation, but the change could also affect Sri Lanka’s place in the competition.Sri Lanka had been selected to host the inaugural women’s Champions Trophy, but the ICC is now expected to move the event to another country. The new venue has not yet been decided and could be discussed at the ICC’s next board meeting.Prakash Shaffter, Secretary of the SLC Transformation Committee, confirmed the change, saying, “Yes, it has been moved out of Sri Lanka. It will be played at another venue, but as of now, I am not sure where it will be played.”The decision could also cause a financial setback for Sri Lanka Cricket. More importantly, Sri Lanka’s women’s team could lose its automatic place in the tournament. The event was planned to include the top five ranked teams along with the host country. Sri Lanka are currently ranked sixth.Sri Lanka Cricket is currently being managed by a government-appointed Transformation Committee.The committee was created to oversee reforms, including changes to the board’s constitution and governance system.However, the ICC has not recognised the politically appointed interim administration. “The ICC does not recognise politically appointed interim administrations and has refused to allow SLC representatives to attend ICC Board meetings since the Transformation Committee took over,” the report said.In July, the ICC said, “The ICC Board received an update on Sri Lanka Cricket and noted progress towards a revised Constitution.”“It reiterated the need for elections to be held as soon as possible and agreed that Sri Lanka Cricket would continue to be unable to be represented at ICC Board meetings for the time being.”The proposed constitutional changes still need to complete the legal process before reaching Parliament, meaning Sri Lanka’s return to an elected administration could take time.The ICC had taken similar action in 2023, when Sri Lanka lost the hosting rights for the 2024 U-19 World Cup after its elected cricket administration was dissolved and replaced with an interim committee.

Article Title: Bizarre! Cricket team loses match due to broken print - here's how
Article Text:
Cricket accessories (AFP Photo)

Home team penalised under strict regulations

A broken printer has resulted in a cricket team conceding a match in Northern Ireland, turning what looked like a normal rain interruption into a highly unusual defeat.Ballyspallen were playing at home against Eglinton in the North West Cricket Union Premier League on Saturday. Eglinton had been bowled out for 159 runs in 48.1 overs and Ballyspallen had started their chase. The hosts had scored 19 runs after two overs when rain stopped play.Because of the weather, the number of overs in the match was expected to be reduced. Officials therefore needed to use the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method, which is used in cricket to work out a revised target when rain interrupts a limited-overs match.However, the required DLS sheet could not be produced because Ballyspallen's printer was not working. Without the document, officials could not continue the match under the competition's rules.Eglinton were consequently awarded the victory, even though not another ball was bowled after the rain delay. The unusual decision was based on the North West Cricket Union's regulations, which specifically cover situations where a DLS calculation cannot be provided.According to the rules, the team hosting the match must immediately concede if a DLS sheet cannot be produced for both teams and the umpires.The regulations also clearly state that the home club should have "a computer loaded with the necessary software, a compatible and operational printer with a sufficient supply of paper and ink, and a proficient operator".The NWCU further says this equipment must be "operational" before the match starts. Ballyspallen's failure to meet that requirement therefore proved costly.The technical problem denied Ballyspallen the opportunity to continue their chase and potentially secure their fifth Premier League victory. Instead, Eglinton took the points without having to bowl another delivery, while Ballyspallen remain at the bottom of the league table.
Article Summary: Ballyspallen were playing at home against Eglinton in the North West Cricket Union Premier League on Saturday. The hosts had scored 19 runs after two overs when rain stopped play. However, the required DLS sheet could not be produced because BallySpallen's printer was not working. Without the document, officials could not continue the match under the competition's rules.

NEW DELHI: Deepti Sharma scripted history on Sunday, producing one of the most remarkable bowling spells in Women’s T20I cricket to become the highest wicket-taker in the format as India began their Women’s T20 Asia Cup campaign with a thumping 94-run victory over Thailand in Dubai.Playing her landmark 150th T20I, Deepti claimed three wickets without conceding a single run from seven deliveries, taking her career tally to 171 wickets and moving past Thailand’s Thipatcha Putthawong, who took one wicket in the match to reach 170 wickets.The veteran all-rounder first drew level with Putthawong when she took two wickets in the ninth over to leave Thailand reeling at 44/6. She returned in the 17th over and struck with her very first delivery, dismissing wicketkeeper-batter Nannapat Koncharoenkai to complete a stunning 3/0.Thailand were eventually bowled out for just 65 in 16.1 overs, giving India a winning start to their campaign.Deepti's achievement was made even more remarkable by the fact that she became the first Indian bowler to claim three or more wickets without conceding a run in a Women's T20I. Overall, there have now been 26 such spells in the format.Her figures of 3/0 are also the best for an Indian bowler taking at least three wickets in a T20I.Renuka Singh previously held the record for the fewest runs conceded with 3/5 against Sri Lanka in Sylhet in 2022.Deepti's three wickets also took her past Putthawong at the top of the global wicket-taking charts. She now has 171 wickets, followed by Putthawong on 170, Rwanda's Henriette Ishimwe on 164 and England's Sophie Ecclestone on 154.The landmark came on a memorable day for Deepti, who had earlier become only the third Indian after Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana to reach 150 T20I appearances.Before Deepti's record-breaking intervention, Shafali Verma had provided India with a flying start. The opener smashed 64 from 36 balls, hitting eight fours and three sixes, and brought up her 19th T20I half-century from just 26 deliveries.India raced past 100 in 10 overs and appeared set for a total in excess of 200. However, Thailand fought back through leg-spinner Suleeporn Laomi , whose variations triggered a dramatic Indian collapse.India slipped from 108/2 to 137/9, losing seven wickets for only 29 runs. Laomi finished with impressive figures of 3/26, including the wickets of Shafali and Richa Ghosh in successive deliveries. Off-spinner Sunida Chaturongrattana added 2/31.Smriti Mandhana had earlier scored 19 from 10 balls before being run out by a direct hit from Aphisara Suwanchonrathi. Pratika Rawal, making her T20I debut in place of injured Jemimah Rodrigues, contributed 22 from 18 balls before Laomi cleaned her up.Despite the collapse, India managed 159/9, with Kranti Gaud's unbeaten 15 off eight balls providing a late boost.Thailand's chase never got going. Kranti Gaud and Nandani Sharma removed the openers early, while Shree Charani and Deepti then dismantled the middle order. Charani finished with 2/10 and Nandani took 3/18.Nannapat offered the only significant resistance with 41, but Deepti ended her stay with the first ball of her final over.The comprehensive win gives India two points to begin their Group A campaign. They next face Hong Kong on Thursday.

Article Title: ENG vs PAK 2nd Test: England thrash Pakistan by 194 runs at Lord’s to take an unassailable 2-0 series lead

England completed an emphatic 194-run victory over Pakistan at Lord’s on Sunday, wrapping up the second Test inside four days to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. The result also ended England’s wait for a Test series victory, with their previous series win coming in December 2024.Set a daunting 389 for victory, Pakistan were bowled out for 194 around 45 minutes after tea, continuing a miserable batting campaign in which they have failed to reach 200 even once in the series. England needed only 18 wickets to win the Test after Pakistan opener Imam-ul-Haq was ruled out of the remainder of the match after tearing his left calf on the opening day.The third and final Test will be played in Birmingham from September 9, but the series result is already beyond Pakistan’s reach.Ollie Robinson was the standout performer for England, producing another superb spell of seam bowling to finish with eight wickets in the match. He took 4/24 on Sunday and ended with remarkable match figures of 8/35, repeatedly troubling Pakistan's batters with his control and movement.Jofra Archer (2/73) also played a key role, combining his raw pace with Robinson's skill and making an important contribution to Pakistan's collapse. Josh Tongue completed the demolition job with three wickets as England cleaned up the tail.Pakistan had begun the fourth day at 14/3 and needed something extraordinary to stay alive in the chase. Saud Shakeel provided it for a while, producing the most substantial innings by a Pakistan batter in the series.Shakeel and Shan Masood put together a stubborn 97-run partnership that frustrated England for almost four hours. Shakeel eventually fell for 97, caught on the boundary while attempting to reach his century, ending the highest individual score by either side in the series.Shakeel had taken the attack to England after lunch, reaching his half-century from 54 balls before continuing to counterattack against the pace attack. He appeared increasingly comfortable against the short ball and began taking risks with the tailenders for company.Masood, who scored 26, concentrated on occupying the crease during their partnership, while Shakeel provided most of the attacking strokes. Their resistance finally ended when Robinson returned with wicketkeeper Jamie Smith standing up to the stumps.Masood was initially given not out after missing an inswinger, but England reviewed the decision and secured the lbw verdict. Robinson then removed Mohammad Rizwan for one to claim his 99th Test wicket before Josh Tongue and the rest of the attack finished the innings.Shakeel's dismissal for 97 summed up Pakistan's batting problems: he had shown the application and skill required to resist England, but there was virtually no support around him.With Imam unable to bat again, Pakistan's hopes disappeared completely. England's bowlers needed little time to wrap up the tail, triggering celebrations and handshakes at Lord's.The victory gives England an unassailable series lead with one Test still to play, while Pakistan must now regroup before the final match in Birmingham on September 9. For England, it was a statement win and their first Test series triumph since December 2024.
Article Summary: England beat Pakistan by 194 runs to win the second Test at Lord's. Ollie Robinson took 8/35 as Pakistan were bowled out for 194. The victory gives England an unassailable 2-0 series lead. The third and final Test is in Birmingham from September 9.

Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off it

Manipur still talking about 2023

Rajasthan: 14 years and counting

Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy picture

And then come Tamil Nadu and others

The ones somewhere in the middle

How active are states/UTs with CWG medallists in promoting sport

Does it matter so much?

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.

Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals.
